passage: At two in the morning in the college hostel, Swati woke to a strange sound. Her roommate Avni was sitting up in bed, gasping, clutching her chest. "I can't breathe. I'm dying. Swati, I'm dying." Swati's own heart leapt into her throat. For a second she wanted to scream for the whole corridor. She didn't. She switched on the small lamp, not the tube light, and sat on the edge of Avni's bed. "I'm here. I'm not going anywhere." Her voice shook, so she slowed it down. "Breathe out with me. Long and slow." It took a long time. Slowly Avni's breaths lengthened. She cried, then went quiet. In the morning Swati walked her to the campus health centre and waited while the doctor saw her. Afterwards she messaged the warden so someone else knew too.

qa.q: What did Swati switch on instead of the tube light?
qa.a: The small lamp.

qa.q: How did Swati feel when she saw Avni gasping, and what shows it?
qa.a: She was frightened too; her heart leapt into her throat and her voice shook.

qa.q: Which of Swati's choices gave Avni an anchor?
qa.a: She stayed calm on the outside, sat close, slowed her voice and breathed with Avni, then took her to the health centre next morning.

qa.q: What might the night have been like for Avni if Swati had panicked too?
qa.a: Avni would likely have felt even more frightened, with no steady person to hold on to.

grounding: It shows a roommate who is scared while witnessing a panic attack, stays steady and kind to anchor her roommate, and arranges follow-up care.

passage: Dear Elizabeth, I'm writing because I'm better with words on paper, and because I don't think I said the right things on Saturday. When I found you on the kitchen floor, shaking and gasping, I was more frightened than I've ever been. I thought something was terribly wrong with your heart. My hands were trembling when I sat beside you. I tried not to let you see. I remember saying, "I'm right here, love. It's going to pass." I don't know if that helped. It seemed to, a little, when your breathing slowed. I've been reading since. I want to go with you to the doctor on Tuesday, if you'll let me, so we can find out what help there is. And if it happens again, I'll be the same steady old dad on the floor beside you. All my love, Dad (Francis)

qa.q: Where did Francis find Elizabeth on Saturday?
qa.a: On the kitchen floor, shaking and gasping.

qa.q: How did Francis feel on finding Elizabeth, and what did Francis try to hide?
qa.a: Francis was more frightened than ever, and tried not to let Elizabeth see the trembling hands.

qa.q: What follow-up step does Francis offer in the letter?
qa.a: Francis offers to go with Elizabeth to the doctor on Tuesday to find out what help there is.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth feel reading that Dad was frightened too?
qa.a: Elizabeth may feel less alone and more loved, knowing Dad stayed steady despite being afraid.

grounding: A father writes about feeling scared while witnessing a child's panic attack, staying steady and kind as an anchor, and wanting follow-up care.

passage: The storm knocked out the power across Chennai, and Keerthana's phone was on four per cent. Her younger brother Tejas, twenty, suddenly clutched his chest on the sofa, gasping. "I can't breathe. Something's wrong. Akka, I'm dying." Keerthana's own heart jumped into her throat. For a second she wanted to scream. Instead she lit a candle, sat beside him and kept her voice low and slow. "I'm here. This is panic. It's horrible, and it will pass. Breathe out with me, long." She didn't rush him or argue. Rain hammered the windows. After some minutes his breathing eased and he slumped against her, shaking. The next morning, she went with him to the doctor, and they asked about seeing a counsellor too.

qa.q: How much charge did Keerthana's phone have?
qa.a: It was on four per cent.

qa.q: How did Keerthana feel when Tejas started gasping?
qa.a: She was frightened, her own heart jumping, and for a second she wanted to scream.

qa.q: What did Keerthana do that gave Tejas an anchor?
qa.a: She stayed steady and kind, lit a candle, sat close, spoke slowly and breathed with him, then took him to the doctor the next morning.

qa.q: How might Tejas have felt when Keerthana stayed calm beside him?
qa.a: He may have felt safer and less alone, which helped him slump against her as the panic eased.

grounding: Shows a sister who feels scared seeing her brother gasping in panic, stays steady and kind as his anchor, and follows up with care, despite a storm and power cut.

passage: At the dinner table in their Kolkata flat, Bidisha, twenty, dropped her spoon and grabbed the table edge. Her breath came in short gasps. "Baba, my heart, I can't..." Ramesh felt terror shoot through him; his first thought was to shout for the neighbours. He stopped himself. He pulled his chair next to hers and put his hand flat on the table near hers, not grabbing. "I'm right here, Bidisha. Look at me. Slow breath out." His voice shook only a little. He didn't fire questions at her. Slowly her grip loosened. Later, alone on the balcony, Ramesh let his own hands tremble. The next day he booked an appointment with their family doctor and went with her.

qa.q: What did Bidisha grab at the dinner table?
qa.a: She grabbed the table edge.

qa.q: How did Ramesh feel when Bidisha began gasping?
qa.a: He felt terrified, his first thought being to shout for the neighbours.

qa.q: What did Ramesh do that helped Bidisha?
qa.a: He stayed calm, sat beside her, spoke slowly without questions, and the next day took her to the family doctor.

qa.q: How might Bidisha have seen her father during the attack?
qa.a: She may have felt anchored by his steady voice and hand, even though he was scared too.

grounding: Shows a parent frightened by his daughter's panic attack who stays steady and kind as her anchor and arranges follow-up care.

passage:
"Vaibhav? Vaibhav, what's happening?"
"Can't breathe. Imran, I think I'm dying."
"Okay. I'm here. I'm sitting right next to you." Imran's hands were shaking. He sat on the floor by the bed. "I think this is panic. It feels awful, but it passes. I'm not going anywhere."
"What if it doesn't stop?"
"It will. Breathe out slow. Like blowing out a candle. With me."
A long silence, just breathing.
"It's easing."
"Good. Good." Imran let out his own breath. "Honestly, you scared me."
"Sorry."
"Don't be sorry. But tomorrow, health centre. I'll come with you."
"Okay."

qa.q: What did Imran tell Vaibhav to breathe like?
qa.a: Like blowing out a candle.

qa.q: How did Imran feel during Vaibhav's attack?
qa.a: He was scared, his hands shaking, though he kept his voice steady.

qa.q: What made Imran's response helpful?
qa.a: He stayed close, spoke calmly, said it would pass without arguing, and planned to go with Vaibhav to the health centre the next day.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav have felt when Imran said he wasn't going anywhere?
qa.a: Vaibhav may have felt reassured and less alone, which helped the panic ease.

grounding: Shows a roommate scared by a friend's panic attack who stays steady and kind, giving an anchor, and follows up with care.

passage:
I'm Joseph, and I shared a flat with Ira in our second year of college in Pune. I still remember the night in October.
I woke to a strange sound. Ira was sitting on the kitchen floor, gasping, her hands clawing at her chest. "I'm dying," she kept saying.
My own heart started hammering. I wanted to scream for the neighbours. Instead I sat down across from her, not too close, and made my voice slow. "I'm here. You're safe. Breathe out with me." I said it again and again, feeling anything but calm inside.
It passed. She cried, and I made us both tea.
The next morning I didn't just leave it. I walked with her to the campus health centre and waited outside. Looking back, I think my steadiness mattered more than any words.

qa.q: Where was Ira sitting when Joseph woke up?
qa.a: On the kitchen floor.

qa.q: How did Joseph feel while helping Ira?
qa.a: Joseph felt scared, heart hammering and wanting to scream for the neighbours, but chose to stay slow and steady on the outside.

qa.q: What did Joseph do that other roommates could learn from?
qa.a: Stay close but not crowding, speak slowly and kindly as an anchor, and follow up the next day by going with the person to get care.

qa.q: How might Ira have experienced Joseph's steady voice?
qa.a: She probably felt less alone and had something to hold on to while she was terrified.

grounding: Joseph sees roommate Ira gasping and terrified, feels scared too, stays steady and kind as an anchor, and follows up with care the next day.
